title: add RAG templates, agent/tool-calling quickstarts, and docs site updates
author: Ava Morgan
description: Summary: Add a set of RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) templates, agent/tool-calling quickstarts in both Python and TypeScript, and updates to the docs site navigation and examples index. Motivation: make it easy for engineers to get started with agent-style tool-calling and RAG patterns using Redwood's API; provide copy-pasteable examples and checklist-driven quickstarts for common patterns (single-doc RAG, multi-doc retrieval pipeline, agent tool-calling with function signatures and structured output). What changed: - New quickstart pages under /docs/quickstarts/rag-and-agents.md with step-by-step instructions and runnable snippets. - Example code in examples/agents/{python,typescript} showing: 1) RAG with vector store integration (FAISS placeholder), 2) agent that calls an external search tool and a structured JSON builder tool, and 3) error-handling and fallback policy examples. - RAG template YAMLs (docs/templates/rag/*.yaml) for customers to copy into Dedicated/Private deployments. - Docs site updates: sidebar ordering, new cards on the quickstarts index, and link-checker exclusions for third-party example assets. - Small accessibility and copy edits across the RAG docs. Checklist (done): - [x] Add quickstart pages and TOC entries - [x] Add runnable Python example and tests - [x] Add TypeScript sample and test harness - [x] Add RAG template YAMLs and example config - [x] Update mkdocs.yml sidebar and quickstarts index - [x] Run link-check and fix broken example links - [x] Tests: docs build + example unit tests pass Related: ENG-6210 (RAG infrastructure work), ENG-6633 (agent runtime enhancements). Links: docs quickstart preview http://staging.docs.internal/quickstarts/rag-and-agents (internal), example repo cross-ref redwood-examples/tree/main/agents. Notes: The examples use a small local FAISS stub for tests; we intentionally left production connector sections as comments so the quickstart remains runnable in CI without cloud dependencies. Migration/Upgrade notes: none required for existing users; templates are additive and behind a docs-only feature flag.
